c.tagline: Red phone boxes, roaring winds, and king penguins just past the last streetlamp

card: Visa/Mastercard widely accepted at hotels, the Malvina House Hotel, larger restaurants, and shops in Stanley; carry FKP or GBP cash (they're interchangeable) for taxis, pubs, and small vendors — US dollars aren't used locally and must be exchanged at Stanley's bank
rides: None — no Uber, Lyft, or ride-hailing apps operate in the Falklands; call a local taxi firm directly (Stanley Cabs, Bonners Taxis, Town Taxis, or Simon's Taxis)

taxi.color: Unmarked private cars/minivans, no standard livery or roof light
taxi.fare: ~$8–12 flat fare for most trips within Stanley
taxi.fareNote: No meters — fares are fixed or agreed in advance; a transfer to/from Mount Pleasant Airport runs roughly $110–150 one-way and should be booked ahead

emergency.police: 999 (islands-wide emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance)
emergency.medical: 999 for emergencies; King Edward VII Memorial Hospital in Stanley for routine and urgent care
emergency.note: Crime is exceptionally rare; 999 is answered locally and response is fast given the small population

religion: Other Christian (United Free, Lutheran, Jehovah's Witness, etc.) ~10%

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: Stanley is small and entirely walkable — the town center along Ross Road can be crossed end to end in under 20 minutes, and nearly every waterfront sight, pub, and shop sits within a few blocks of the harbour.

safety.safety: One of the safest places in the world to travel; violent crime against visitors is essentially unheard of
safety.crime: Extremely low; petty theft is rare, many residents leave doors unlocked, and there is no history of crime targeting tourists

hood_landmark.West Stanley: Stanley Cemetery & St. Mary's Catholic Church

hood_desc: The compact harbourfront core, lined with brightly painted cottages, pubs, gift shops, and the town's main jetty where cruise tenders land.
The genteel eastern stretch of Ross Road facing the harbour, home to the Governor's residence and several of Stanley's guesthouses.
The quieter dockyard quarter east of downtown, anchored by the Falkland Islands Museum and old naval buildings, with harbor views.
A residential hillside area west of the center with the cemetery, church, and modest houses climbing away from the water.
The town's outer edge toward the airport road, gateway to Gypsy Cove, Yorke Bay, and the wider camp (countryside) beyond.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink.

transit.sys: None — Stanley has no public bus, tram, or rail system
transit.pay: N/A — get around on foot, by private taxi, or rental 4x4
transit.note: There is no formal public transit in Stanley or anywhere in the Falklands; the town is small enough to walk everywhere, and local taxi firms (plus rental cars) cover trips beyond downtown, including the long haul out to Mount Pleasant Airport.

transport.air: The only practical way in: fly to RAF Mount Pleasant Airport (MPN), about 35 mi/58 km from Stanley — served by a weekly LATAM flight from Punta Arenas, Chile (via Santiago), and a twice-weekly RAF/civilian charter from RAF Brize Norton, UK, routing via Ascension Island.
transport.train: No railways exist anywhere in the Falkland Islands.
transport.bus: No scheduled public bus service in Stanley; a coach/shuttle meets international flights at Mount Pleasant to transfer passengers to Stanley.
transport.ferry: No scheduled passenger ferry service to Stanley; the harbour is a major Antarctic and South American cruise-ship stop, with passengers tendered ashore at the Public Jetty and FIPASS.
transport.car: Rental cars and 4x4s are available in Stanley and are essential for reaching Gypsy Cove, Volunteer Point, and other outlying sights, since most roads outside town are unpaved gravel tracks.

airport.name: RAF Mount Pleasant Airport (Mount Pleasant Complex)
airport.distance: ~35 miles (58 km) southwest of Stanley, about 1–1.5 hours by road
airport.transport: Pre-booked private transfer/taxi (roughly $110–150 one-way) or a coach shuttle timed to flight arrivals; rental car pickup available at the airport terminal; no walk-up taxi rank or public bus at MPA

net.m: Sure South Atlantic is the sole mobile operator; 4G covers Stanley and nearby areas, with prepaid SIM cards sold locally
net.w: Wi-Fi is available at hotels, guesthouses, and cafés in Stanley but is often slow and data-capped
net.ops: Sure South Atlantic (the territory's only telecom and internet provider)
net.gb: Mobile data is costly and sold in small bundles, roughly $15–25 per GB
net.fwn: Connectivity runs via a 2013 subsea fibre link supplemented by satellite capacity; free wifi is limited outside hotels
net.ap: Overseas roaming is very expensive; buying a local Sure SIM on arrival at Stanley or the airport is the practical option

tip.s: Tipping is not customary or expected anywhere in the Falkland Islands, in keeping with British practice.
tip.r: Restaurants: rounding up or adding 5–10% for standout service is appreciated but never required; taxis are never tipped.
